standard_prerequisites.name: The adjunction defining extension by zero and the relation g^{-1}G(U) = G(u(U))

standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the two identifications that make the Hom-set computation work.

standard_prerequisites.name: Continuity and cocontinuity of the functor u
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Sites, section on continuous and cocontinuous functors
standard_prerequisites.use: Ensures that the associated morphism of topoi g has the stated properties used in the computation.

core_obligations: For an object U and a module G on the target, compute the Hom-set from the standard generator j_{U!}O_U into g^{-1}G and identify it successively with g^{-1}G(U), with G(u(U)), and with the Hom-set from j_{u(U)!}O_{u(U)} into G (proof lines 8236-8250).

Use these identifications to define g_! on the standard generators and conclude that the resulting functor is left adjoint to g^*, extending to arbitrary modules via presentations, completing the proof up to line 8256 (proof lines 8251-8256).
proof_roadmap: Compute Homs out of the standard generators into the pullback.
Identify them with Homs out of the corresponding generators on the target.
Extend by presentations to obtain the left adjoint.
difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs a functor g_! on modules, left adjoint to g^*, for a continuous and cocontinuous functor u between sites when the structure sheaf of the source is the pullback of that of the target. The proof computes the Hom-set from a standard generator j_{U!}O_U into g^{-1}G and identifies it successively with the value of g^{-1}G at U, with G at u(U), and finally with the Hom-set from j_{u(U)!}O_{u(U)} into G, which exhibits the required adjunction; the general case follows by presenting modules by such generators (proof lines 8236-8256). H2: the chain of identifications computing the Hom-sets is the substance and is carried out explicitly.
